newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish state energy firm stakes to stay above 2/3.
newsitem.headline: Finnish state energy firm stakes to stay above 2/3.

text.p: The government does not intend to reduce the state's holdings in energy companies to below two thirds, Trade and Industry Minister Antti Kalliomaki said on Wednesday.
"We do not have any intentions to go below two thirds (ownership) in energy companies during this government's term of office (until spring 1999)," Kalliomaki told Reuters after a news conference.
The state's stake in oil, chemicals and energy group Neste Oy is 83.5 percent and the government has parliament's authorisation to cut it to 50.1 percent.

In power producer Imatran Voima Oy (IVO), the state's direct ownership is 95.6 percent (state-owned Social Insurance Institution KELA owns the rest), and it has authorisation to lower it to 50.1 percent.

"The biggest (privatisation) operations have been made," Kalliomaki told a news conference. Asked specifically about IVO, he said: "I did not say that there could absolutely not be any ownership changes in state companies."
IVO said in March that it could seek a bourse listing in spring next year. The market had earlier looked for an initial public offering from the company towards the end of 1997.

In 1996, the state continued privatising its industrial holdings, reducing its stake in chemicals group Kemira Oy to just under 54 percent, and its ownership of paper machinery group Valmet Oy to about 20 percent, Kalliomaki said, according to a copy of his prepared speech. @

After sales this year of hydropower shares in energy group Kemijoki Oy and an issue and offering in steel group Rautaruukki Oy, state companies had taken in over 7.5 billion markka of risk capital from privatisation moves, he said.
Total state revenues from the privatisation process had amounted to about 9.9 billion, Kalliomaki said.
In 1996, the state-controlled companies paid 1.5 billion markka in dividends to the state, he said.
State-owned firms would continue to seek to pay "comparable" dividends, said Markku Tapio, deputy director general of the ministry of trade and industry. @
